speed_investigation.method: slope-isolated per-decompile cost (load once in one decomp_dbg session, decompile main N times, per-decompile = (T(N2)-T(N1))/(N2-N1); cancels the ~190ms fixed process-spawn/load/SLEIGH-mmap cost). 5-rep median, N1=20 N2=120.
speed_investigation.note_on_wall_clock_delta: The PR-body +34.3% wall-clock figure is the same effect diluted by the shared fixed load; the slope figure above is the honest marginal decompile cost (~2.6x).
speed_investigation.heuristic_cost: kuna_try_guard_bound_table invoked 3x at ~7us each (~22us total, <0.1% of the ON<->OFF gap); 0x with the gate off (confirmed). The new hot-path code is essentially free.
speed_investigation.root_cause: INHERENT and downstream, not algorithmic. With the gate off the BRANCHIND is truncated to a single CALLIND (whole 55-entry switch + getopt while-loop collapse to one computed call); with it on the switch survives, so CFG-build/dataflow/structuring/type-inference process a ~2.6x larger real function. No O(n^2)/O(n^3), no per-op/per-CFG-node recomputation, no repeated dominator/region rebuild. scan_guard_tree is already triple-bounded (64-step walk, 4096-step eval budget, v-loop capped at maxtablesize=1024).
speed_investigation.disposition: No localized algorithmic fix exists; the extra time is correct work. Kept DEFAULT-OFF opt-in (speed_forced_off=true) per the +5% gate, also matching the over-bound risk profile. Output byte-identical with the gate off (675/675 datatests unchanged) -> no docs/divergences.md entry.
speed_investigation.variable_duplication: The 'too many declared variables on top' is NOT from this feature: it is a pre-existing render artifact already mitigated on main by `dedupvardecls` (DIV-7, default-on, landed after this branch). With dedupvardecls off the ON output renders 67x int4 t / 34x int4 m / 34x int4 c / 33x int4 fd; with it on (default) the declaration block is ~12 clean lines. Cause: one stack slot maps onto many un-merged same-named scalar HighVariables (one per loop/switch-phi SSA merge point) and the printer emits one decl per HighVariable. dedupvardecls collapses identical rendered lines (render-side), it does not fix the underlying HighVariable over-fragmentation. The residual `int4 t` x2 is a legitimate sub-piece split (t._0_4_ / t._4_4_ of the 8-byte -0x28 slot), correctly not collapsed. See analysis.md for the follow-up hypothesis (Merge::mergeAdjacent* in s6_merge).

decisions.question: Scope (small vs large) + hook point + default + whether to fix analyzeGuards
decisions.decision: scope: small. It is one gated JumpBasic model-extension method (kuna_try_guard_bound_table) + one new module owning the option/arch-flag, structurally identical to the switchmodbound (GH-9191) precedent: no new pass TYPE, no S7/structuring touch (the BRANCHIND->CALLIND collapse happens in truncate_indirect_jump BEFORE structuring; bound the table and the switch survives), 3 ported-core anchor files (jumptable.rs, architecture.rs, seams.rs) + option-registry files + 1 new module. Hook point CONFIRMED: recover_model_basic's `jrange.size > maxtablesize` failure branch, immediately after the kuna_try_modulo_bound_table check (path_meld/jrange/varnodeIndex already populated; independent `if` branches so neither gate shadows the other). Default-OFF opt-in REGARDLESS of ablation: the guard-to-index correspondence is a control-flow heuristic asserted across a memory round-trip it cannot prove in dataflow, whose worst case is WRONG output (collapsed/spurious cases on an unrelated jump), not just missing output. Do NOT touch analyze_guards: it is verbatim-ported core (deliberately conservative on partial functions via usenzmask = !is_partial); the gated downstream rebound keeps `gate off => upstream byte-identical` (preserved here: 675/675 unchanged) and avoids 675-datatest parity risk. MANDATORY: also wire the ArchSeam flag (seams.rs + build_arch_handle copy) — recover_model_basic runs off the seam handle, so setting the flag only on the real Architecture would never fire (the documented archseam-flags trap; switchmodbound proves it is required).

decisions.question: How to extract the table bound N when the guard is in unsimplified flag form, register-reused (idx and m at the same storage), and the simplifier rewrote `idx > 0x36` into `idx > 0x35 && m != 0x75`
decisions.decision: Constant-aggregation of comparison operands is insufficient (it yields N=0x36, missing the boundary 'u' case at idx 0x36 carried by the `m != 0x75` term). Instead EVALUATE the guard boolean as a function of a candidate index varnode v: pick the meld index var, build a linear-offset map for its register-reused siblings (m = v + 0x3f, from idx's INT_ADD def), concretely evaluate the boolean for v = 0,1,2,... and take N = the first v whose routing flips from v=0's. GCC normalizes the table to start at index 0 (sub LOW), so the switch values form a contiguous prefix [0, N); this correctly composes the `idx > 0x35` and `m != 0x75` terms to N = 0x37 (55). Result on the target: 6 cases + default recovered, fileno present once, no computed call.
